title: Finite adjoin with Jacobson power
statement: Under the hypotheses of semilocal-dim-one-conductor-power, for x,y in the integral closure and x in its Jacobson radical, there exists a finite B-subalgebra A of K with fraction field K containing x and y, and a positive m with an element a of A equal to x^m and lying in the extension of the Jacobson radical of B.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2, adjoin and Jacobson paragraphs

proof.text: Apply the finite adjoin construction to obtain A, its fraction field, generators, and the compatible injective map into the integral closure with surjective prime-spectrum comap. The proof is the existing upstream theorem; the unused dimension-one hypothesis of the retired Sheaf statement is unnecessary.
Apply the integral-overring Jacobson-power theorem to the compatible integral extension and package the resulting power in A.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_adjoin_with_jacobson_power
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Finite (MaximalSpectrum B)]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra B K] [IsFractionRing B K]
    [Finite (MaximalSpectrum (integralClosure B K))]
    (x y : integralClosure B K)
    (hx : x ∈ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal (integralClosure B K))) :
    ∃ A : Subalgebra B K, Module.Finite B A ∧ IsFractionRing A K ∧
      (x : K) ∈ A ∧ (y : K) ∈ A ∧
      ∃ m : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ ∃ a : A,
        (a : K) = (x : K) ^ m ∧
        a ∈ Ideal.map (algebraMap B A) (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B))
lean.note: Retired unused Sheaf twin. The upstream theorem has the same conclusion without the unused ringKrullDim B = 1 hypothesis; direct specialization proves the old statement.
